item.title: Survey for the Establishment of the Experimental Field for the GNSS System Development in the Kingdom of Thailand
item.description:
Period: November 2018 – November 2019

Client: The Government of Thailand

Funded by: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)

Role: Consultant, Kokusai Kogyo Co., Ltd.

Overview

GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) positioning with CORS (Continuously Operating Reference Stations) enables highly accurate positioning, which is the basis of applications such as surveying, precision agriculture and autonomous driving. This survey collected information for establishing an experimental field for GNSS system development in Thailand, including a CORS data centre.

My contribution

  • Surveyed and organized information on the establishment of the CORS data centre.

Skills

GNSS/CORS, geospatial information systems, system survey

item.title: The Project for Strengthening Operation and Maintenance of Rural Water Supply Systems in Rwanda (RWASOM project)
item.description:
Period: June 2018 – December 2019

Client: Water and Sanitation Corporation Ltd. (WASAC), Rwanda

Funded by: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)

Role: GIS Expert, Kokusai Kogyo Co., Ltd.

Overview

The RWASOM project aimed to strengthen the capacity for operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems in Rwanda. Reliable information on where water supply facilities are located and in what condition they are is essential for their operation and maintenance, but it was not available nationwide. I joined the project as a GIS expert to establish a GIS database and data sharing platform for rural water supply management.

Activities

  • Training: Conducted training workshops on data collection and data sharing with FOSS4G applications (QGIS, QField) for Rwandan colleagues.
  • Nationwide mapping: Collaborated with Rwandan colleagues to complete the mapping of all rural water supply systems in the country using QField and Garmin GPS.
  • GIS database: Designed and created a PostGIS database for rural water supply management.
  • Data sharing platform: Developed a data sharing platform using Lizmap/QGIS Server so that the data can be accessed by stakeholders.
  • Sustainability: Used only open-source software so that WASAC can keep operating the system without license costs. The data was later published as vector tiles at rural.water-gis.com.

Related talks

  • FOSS4G 2019: Case study of data collection & data sharing for rural water supply management in Rwanda
  • FOSS4G 2021: An implementation of FOSS4G - QGIS, QField and Vector Tiles for rural water supply management in Rwanda
  • FOSS4G 2022: Rural water supply mapping by using FOSS4G application in Rwanda

Skills

PostGIS, Lizmap/QGIS Server, QGIS Desktop, QField, Garmin GPS, geospatial data collection, training

item.title: Preparatory Survey for the Project for Strengthening Nzove-Ntora Principal Water Transmission Pipeline in Kigali City, Rwanda
item.description:
Period: October 2017 – November 2018

Client: Water and Sanitation Corporation Ltd. (WASAC), Rwanda

Funded by: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)

Role: Consultant, Kokusai Kogyo Co., Ltd.

Overview

The Nzove-Ntora principal transmission pipeline carries treated water from the Nzove Water Treatment Plant to the Ntora reservoir, and is one of the main water supply lines for Kigali City, the capital of Rwanda. This preparatory survey was conducted to plan the upgrade and strengthening of the transmission pipeline, in order to improve the water supply to the growing city.

My contribution

  • Collected and organized geospatial data of the existing water supply facilities and pipelines.
  • Supported the design and planning of the water infrastructure, including hydraulic analysis with EPANET.

Skills

Geospatial data collection, EPANET, water supply, design/planning of water infrastructure, QGIS

item.title: The GIS project in Narok Water, Kenya
item.description:
Period: April 2014 – September 2016

Organization: Narok Water and Sewerage Services Co., Ltd. (NARWASSCO), Kenya

Role: GIS Specialist (JICA Volunteer)

Background

Narok Water and Sewerage Services Co., Ltd. is the water service provider for Narok and Ololulung’a towns in Kenya. Like many water utilities in Eastern Africa, it faced high Non-Revenue Water (NRW), and there were no accurate maps of its water distribution network and customers. I was dispatched as a GIS specialist by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to introduce GIS for water asset and NRW management.

Activities

  • Network mapping: Mapped the entire water distribution network, approximately 300 km of pipelines in total, in Narok and Ololulung’a towns using Trimble GPS, ArcPad and QGIS.
  • GIS database & WebGIS: Designed and developed a GIS database and WebGIS using PostGIS, MapServer and Leaflet. The system is linked to the billing system, which helps improve revenue collection.
  • NRW management: Created DMAs (District Metered Areas) to analyze and improve Non-Revenue Water management.
  • Capacity building: Conducted training to transfer technical knowledge to Kenyan colleagues. The GIS system has been continuously used since it was developed.
  • Consulting for other utilities: Consulted on GIS work for 7 water service providers in Kenya: Nyeri Water, Kabarnet Water, Kapsabet Water, Nakuru Water, Nakuru Rural Water, Naivasha Water and Mavoko Water.

Afterwards

I have kept a personal partnership with Narok Water as a volunteer. The GIS was later modernized with open-source vector tiles (narok.water-gis.com), and the experience was presented at FOSS4G 2019 Bucharest and FOSS4G 2021.

  • FOSS4G 2019: Case study of Non-Revenue Water management of Narok Water in Kenya
  • FOSS4G 2021: The impact of application of FOSS4G on Non-Revenue Water

Skills

Data collection for water infrastructure, WebGIS, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, MapServer, Leaflet, QGIS, EPANET
